proposed.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XII, Sec. 1202, two required exits must be separated by what minimum distance to prevent both from being blocked by a single fire event?

options.text: At least one-half of the diagonal dimension of the floor area served
At least one-fifth (1/5) of the perimeter of the floor area served
At least one-third (1/3) of the longest dimension of the floor area
At least 9.00 m measured in a straight line between exit door centerlines

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Sec. 1202 requires exit separation of at least 1/5 of the perimeter of the floor area served — not the diagonal. The diagonal-based rule (1/2 diagonal) is from US building codes and is a common exam distractor. The 1/5 perimeter rule is specific to PD 1096.
proposed.explanation: The 1/5 perimeter versus 1/2 diagonal distinction is one of the highest-frequency traps on the LEA. US-trained candidates consistently select the diagonal rule. PD 1096 uses the perimeter rule, which produces different minimum distances for non-square floors.
